title: Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management: insights and retention policy recommendations for sensitive SharePoint and OneDrive data
summary: The briefing accurately reports Microsoft's roadmap targets and distinguishes the planned insights from existing retention-policy controls. The documented path, PowerShell call, licences and SharePoint administrator restriction are supported; searches found no documentation establishing the new feature's default, entitlement or controls.

claims.claim: Learn describes retention policies as the cornerstone of Data Lifecycle Management.
claims.quote: Retention policies are the cornerstone for data lifecycle management.

claims.claim: Retention policies cover Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams and Viva Engage.
claims.quote: Use these policies for Microsoft 365 workloads that include Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, and Viva Engage.

claims.claim: Retention policies can retain content.
claims.quote: Configure whether content for these services needs to be retained indefinitely, or for a specific period if users edit or delete it.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A retention policy can be configured to permanently delete content after a specified period.
claims.quote: Or you can configure the policy to automatically permanently delete the content after a specified period if it's not already deleted.

claims.claim: Retention policies can combine retention and subsequent deletion.
claims.quote: You can also combine these two actions for retain and then delete, which is a very typical configuration.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Compliance Administrator role group is a documented way to grant permission to create and manage retention policies.
claims.quote: To grant permissions for this limited administration, we recommend that you add users to the Compliance Administrator admin role group.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: A custom role group with the Retention Management role is an alternative for retention-policy administration.
claims.quote: Alternatively to using this default role, you can create a new role group and add the Retention Management role to this group.

claims.claim: View-Only Retention Management is the documented read-only role.
claims.quote: For a read-only role, use View-Only Retention Management.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Administrators assigned administrative units cannot configure policies including SharePoint sites; an unrestricted administrator is required.
claims.quote: if you're a restricted administrator assigned one or more adminsitrative units, you won't be able to configure a retention policy that includes SharePoint sites or Exchange public folders. For these locations, you must be an unrestricted administrator.

claims.claim: The person configuring retention policies does not require access to the content.
claims.quote: These permissions are required only to create, configure, and apply retention policies and retention labels. The person configuring these policies and labels doesn't require access to the content.

claims.claim: Priority Cleanup Admin is a separate role required for priority cleanup.
claims.quote: admins must have the Priority Cleanup Admin role. This role isn't included by default in the Compliance Administrator admin role group.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Existing retention policies are reached in Microsoft Purview portal through Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies, with New retention policy starting creation.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies. Select New retention policy to start the Create retention policy configuration, and name your new retention policy.

claims.claim: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Name "<policy name>" -SharePointLocation "<site URL>" creates an existing retention-policy object targeting a SharePoint site.
claims.quote: Use the New-RetentionCompliancePolicy cmdlet to create new retention policies and new retention label policies ... The SharePointLocation parameter specifies the SharePoint sites to include. You identify the site by its URL value

claims.claim: A new retention policy is not valid until a rule is added, and scripting therefore also needs New-RetentionComplianceRule.
claims.quote: Policies are not valid until a rule is added (for retention policies) or a label is added (for retention label policies). ... The next step is to use the New-RetentionComplianceRule cmdlet to add a rule to the retention policy.

claims.claim: The second control row describes existing retention-policy creation rather than a control over the new insights.
claims.quote: Use a retention policy to manage the data for your organization by deciding proactively whether to retain content, delete content, or retain and then delete the content.
